chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), who said:
I would wish that I could ransom two characteristics in the Shi'a for some [flesh] of my forearm: impatience (al-nuzq) and scarcity of keeping secrets (qillat al-kitman).

key_terms.النُّزْق: Impatience, hasty temper, or quickness to anger

ai.seo_question: What are the two main negative characteristics of the Shi'a mentioned in this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) highlights 'al-nuzq' (hasty, impetuous behavior) and 'qillat al-kitman' (inability to keep secrets) as critical flaws within the Shi'a community. His expression of wishing to 'ransom' these traits underscores their detrimental impact on both individual spiritual integrity and the collective political prudence (taqiyyah) essential for the survival of the Shi'a identity. This narration serves as a foundational ethical guideline for balancing outward expression with inward discretion in Shia scholarly tradition.
